family.shared_definition: a large flat dish or board used for serving food and beverages
family.neutral_stem: Carrying refreshments into the dining room, he balanced
family.semantic_notes: Platter specifically denotes a broad serving plate for food, whereas tray denotes a rimmed flat surface used to carry multiple items.

source_context_dev: The buffet centerpiece required expansive surface area to showcase the assortment of cheeses and cured meats.
An elaborate cold buffet arrangement demanded maximum diameter to display every delicacy without overlap.
The chef had prepared a sprawling spread of hors d'oeuvres that spread outward across a broad circumference.
Setting up the banquet required an expansive spread that could hold several rows of appetizers side by side.
target_context_dev: The dinner service involved thick stone vessels and cast-iron cookware that strained his forearms.
Multiple iron dishes and dense pewter flagons made transportation unusually strenuous for the server.
Dense crystal decanters and thick stoneware mugs added tremendous mass to the evening order.
He felt the severe downward pull from several dense ceramic bowls full of hot soup.
source_context_test: The host insisted on an expansive layout so guests could view every single pastry at a glance.
Accommodating dozens of sliced canapés required an unusually expansive diameter.

target_context_test: Shifting the full iron tureen and several solid ceramic jugs demanded immense wrist strength.

constructions.semantic_audit_notes: All combinations (wide platter, wide tray, heavy platter, heavy tray) are grammatically correct and semantically valid in hospitality contexts. Source contexts emphasize horizontal expanse and broad surface spread; target contexts emphasize physical heft and dense cookware.
